children: The dollar trades steady as investors await U.S. consumer-price inflation data at 1230 GMT, the final key data ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting next week. The dollar rose Thursday, driven by rising oil prices and stronger-than-expected producer-price inflation figures increasing prospects of an interest-rate rise. However, even if Friday's inflation figures are strong, Fed policymakers could point to moderating core inflation and opt to hold rates steady next week, Commerzbank's Michael Pfister says. "Even if today's figure sends a clear signal, this does not necessarily mean that the Fed (and thus the dollar) will ultimately pick it up," he says. The DXY dollar index is steady at 99.051, having risen to 99.199 on Thursday. (jessica.fleetham@wsj.com)
